There is nothing but the miracle - what else do these words emptiness, God, mystery point to? That the awe of the miraculous comes to be buried in the inertia of normality, of familiarity, is perhaps the greatest mystery of all. The desultory succor of chancing assumptions and glancing, approbating persuasions is no balm for the nameless spirit, but a crutch for the mind; and only so when the mind forgets what truly walks in its shoes. For what walks, when the mind is at a standstill, is the miracle in flight, none other than the wind itself. Yet in poetry and principle come these wings to the mind's wandering, like the feet of our dear Hermes, so out upon the world the miracle may flock and intone, to raze the familiar, and raise all familiars to the sky.
